notes: Cross-match: Table 1 names were matched to Gaia EDR3 identifiers through the shared object number (#) in Table A.1, as stated in the table notes. B576(a) denotes the single star B576; the (a) footnote marks a blue horizontal branch star. J0136+2425 is the short name for SDSS J013655.91+242546.0. Where a star both was a previous candidate and is retained here as a current unbound candidate, I list it once as candidates_found (e.g. S5-HVS 1, HVS 5, HVS 6, LAMOST HVS 1, LAMOST HVS 4). Status ambiguity: T:p4-b3 calls S5-HVS 1 the 'only object' gravitationally unbound, whereas T:p1-b6, T:p4-b6, T:p4-b10 and T:p5-b3 explicitly call HVS 5 and/or HVS 6 unbound. I treated the T:p4-b3 wording as restricted to the three GC-origin candidates and followed the repeated explicit statements for HVS 5 and HVS 6. I treated the paper's 'hyper-runaway' class as Galactic-unbound disk-origin status because T:p1-b12 defines it through the gravitationally unbound HD 271791. The model-dependent hyper-runaway status of LAMOST HVS 2, J0136+2425 and HVS 8 in T:p4-b6, and the statement in T:p4-b10 that B481 and HVS 7 'might be' unbound, were treated as accepted conditional candidacy and entered as candidates_found. Prior-candidate group: the paper describes the 14 MMT-HVS program stars collectively as coming from the MMT-HVS survey and identifies its historical candidate HVSs at T:p1-b10 and T:p2-b1; I therefore treated the now-bound MMT-HVS program stars B537, B576, B598, B434, B733, B711, HVS 17, B485 and B143 as follow_up using group-level evidence. The paper does not individually enumerate which of the 40 revised MMT-HVS stars correspond to every historical candidate, so this link is group-level rather than a per-star prior statement. LAMOST HVS 3 is follow_up as one of the four explicitly identified LAMOST candidate HVSs; HD 271791 and HIP 60350 are follow_up because the text reports their earlier unbound/potential-hyper-runaway status at T:p1-b12 and T:p2-b4. Excluded boundary cases: PG 1610+062 (Gaia EDR3 4450123955938796160) is called an extreme disk-runaway, not explicitly a Galactic-unbound candidate, and HVS 22 (Gaia EDR3 3897063727354575488) is explicitly outside the current sample at T:p4-b4 without a retained current/prior unbound candidacy in the supplied text.

S5-HVS 1: Target identified by row 1 of Tables 1, A.1, and A.2: S5-HVS 1 = Gaia EDR3 6513109241989477504. I retain the present-day galactocentric radius r=8.52 kpc rather than the plane-crossing radius r_p=0.19 kpc, because the requested galactocentric_radius is defined for the present-day state and excludes cylindrical radius. Table A.2 also gives v_Grf,p=1760 km/s and v_ej=1810 km/s at plane crossing; these are not the present-day Galactic rest-frame speed and ejection velocity is not among the requested quantities, so they are not entered here. The paper explicitly tabulates only P_b=0% and describes S5-HVS 1 as gravitationally unbound; it does not separately tabulate an unbound probability, so I did not derive one. No RA, Dec, parallax, or proper-motion components are tabulated for the target in the supplied material.

B537: Target: B537, identified in Table 1 as object #2 and by Gaia EDR3 identifier 2799690344752115584. RA, Dec, parallax, and proper-motion components are not reported in the supplied tables or text, so they are not extracted. Table A.2 lists both present-day Galactocentric quantities (r, v_Grf) and plane-intersection quantities (r_p, v_Grf,p); both distinct results are retained with conditions. Table A.2 gives P_b = 100 (per cent) for #2; no uncertainty is tabulated. Unbound probability is not explicitly reported and is not derived.

B576: B576 is marked (a) in Table 1 at T:p2-b5 as a blue horizontal branch star, and T:p4-b3 states that the nature of B576 and B598 is not yet clear. Table A.2 at T:p9-b0 provides current r and v_Grf; its plane-crossing values r_p and v_Grf,p were not entered under galactocentric_radius or galactic_rest_frame_velocity because the rules call for the present-day state. No right ascension, declination, parallax, or proper-motion components are tabulated in the supplied material.

B598: Target B598 is object #4 (Gaia EDR3 1225026618163072512) in Tables 1, A.1, and A.2 (T:p2-b5, T:p8-b0, T:p9-b0). The tabulated r_p = 1.0 kpc is the galactocentric radius at plane intersection, not the present-day radius, so only the present-day r = 20.7 kpc is recorded for galactocentric_radius. The paper does not tabulate equatorial coordinates, parallax, or proper-motion components for this object, so those quantities are omitted.

HVS 5: HVS 5 is row 5 of Tables 1, A.1, and A.2 (Gaia EDR3 1069326945513133952). The paper gives P_b = 0% and describes HVS 5 as gravitationally unbound (T:p4-b6), but does not report a separate numerical unbound probability; I did not derive one. Table A.2 also lists the past plane-crossing radius r_p = 9.5 kpc, which is not used for the present-day galactocentric radius. No right ascension, declination, parallax, or proper-motion components are tabulated.

HVS 6: No equatorial coordinates, parallax, or proper-motion components are numerically reported for HVS 6 in the supplied material. Table A.2 also lists r_p = 25^{+6}_{-6} kpc at plane intersection (T:p9-b0; Table 1 at T:p2-b5), but this is a past plane-crossing quantity and not the present-day galactocentric radius. The paper states that HVS 6 is gravitationally unbound (T:p4-b10, T:p5-b3), and Table A.2 gives P_b = 0% (T:p9-b0); no separate numerical unbound probability is tabulated.

B481: Target B481 is object #7 (Gaia EDR3 2660715403600483584). The supplied paper does not report equatorial coordinates, parallax, or proper-motion components; only the Gaia EDR3 identifier is tabulated (I:p8-b0). Table A.2 also gives plane-crossing (past-state) r_p = 29^{+7}_{-10} kpc and v_Grf,p = 476^{+28}_{-16} km/s (I:p9-b0); these were not used for the present-day galactocentric-radius and rest-frame-speed quantities. P_b is reported only as a bound probability (60%); no unbound probability is explicitly tabulated.
